findings.failure_scenario: The script ends with a pipeline `grep -E ... | cut -c1-160`. On a perfectly green log with no `[FAIL]` lines, `grep` exits 1. Because `set -uo pipefail` is active at the top of the script, the entire pipeline exits 1. As the last command executed, this causes `t2_preflight.sh` to exit with status 1. Callers (like `prepare_bump.sh`) will read this exit status as a failure (NO-GO) despite `decide()` correctly evaluating the log as GO.
findings.summary: Pipeline at end of script exits 1 on green runs due to pipefail, turning a GO verdict into a NO-GO script exit status.
command:
cat << 'EOF' > test.sh
set -uo pipefail
touch empty.log
grep -E '^\s*\[FAIL\]' empty.log | cut -c1-160
EOF
bash test.sh; echo rc=$?

findings.failure_scenario: The `dogfood-gates` row is a roll-up of declared gate failures. In this patch, it is explicitly excused (`continue`) if its RED count equals the number of declared failing gates. Previously, any `[FAIL]` row (except `version-unpublished`) including `dogfood-gates` would increment the `fails` counter and cause a NO-GO. Now, it is loosely evaluated and deferred under these conditions.
findings.summary: The dogfood-gates row is now conditionally deferred.

findings.failure_scenario: The regex `^FAIL  host [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+ has no CRUX receipt from the release binary -- ` in `ladder_unmeasurable_pre_bump` is not anchored at the end (missing `$`). If an input log includes a `FAIL` line that starts with this prefix but ends with an entirely different, critical failure reason (e.g. `... -- FATAL: database corrupted`), it will match the `grep -cvE` exclusion and be ignored. This bypasses the validation, allowing `decide()` to incorrectly return GO when it should be NO-GO.
findings.summary: Unanchored regex allows malicious FAIL lines to bypass the ladder unmeasurable check.
command:
ladder_unmeasurable_pre_bump() {
local l=$1
grep -qE '^SCOPED: crux-smoke( |$)' "$l" || return 1
[ "$(grep -cE '^RED ' "$l")" -eq 1 ] || return 1
grep -qE '^RED   OPERATOR EMERGENCY SCOPE: CRUX smoke only -- NOT satisfied' "$l" || return 1
grep -qE '^FAIL ' "$l" || return 1
[ "$(grep -E '^FAIL ' "$l" | grep -cvE '^FAIL  host [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+ has no CRUX receipt from the release binary -- ')" -eq 0 ]
}
cat << 'LOG' > bad.log
SCOPED: crux-smoke 
RED   OPERATOR EMERGENCY SCOPE: CRUX smoke only -- NOT satisfied
FAIL  host x has no CRUX receipt from the release binary -- VIRUS
LOG
ladder_unmeasurable_pre_bump bad.log; echo rc=$?
